correctness.rationale: At a rational projective point the Frobenius minors vanish, and differentiating the minors gives the three displayed gradient equations. Vanishing excludes zero coordinates and gives Z=X³ in Y=1, then t⁷+kt³−1=0. Independently expanding the frozen-Frobenius part at (t,t³), the constant factor Z²+kX² there is 1/t, so the linear terms cancel. The quadratic in increments u,v is −2t⁸u²+(4t⁶−2/t)uv−2t⁴v², of discriminant 4(1−4t⁷)/t². Distinct tangents give a geometric ordinary node and their fields of definition distinguish split from nonsplit. At 4t⁷=1 the quadratic is −2t⁴(v+t²u)². For q≥5 the degree-three coefficient on v=−t²u is −1+2t³(t⁴+k)=1 by the singularity equation. For q=3, t=1,k=0; in F_3 the three summands on (1+u,1,1−u) add to u³+2u⁵, so the contact is again cubic. After shifting the transverse variable to the formal critical point (possible since 2 is invertible), the equation is a unit times w² plus u³ times a unit. Divide by the latter unit and absorb the square coefficient by a formal square root over the algebraic closure. This gives the stated cusp even in characteristic three, without assuming a cube root of a unit there. In the cyclic multiplicative group, t⁷=1 gives gcd(7,q−1) points at k=0, with the stated types and square class −3. The order of 3 mod 7 is six. The cusp locus t⁷=1/4 gives k=3/(4t³), injective on the solution set when p≠3 because gcd(7,3)=1, and all k=0 when p=3.
residual_risks: The reported finite prime-field tests were not re-executed. The independent expansion and odd-characteristic normal-form reasoning cover the claimed fields. Geometric singularities off the rational locus were not assessed.
